A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FCA research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite substantial layout changes and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original FCA benchmark results, design ablations, qualitative predictions, VBench scores, and a human evaluation. These are distinguishable from baseline results attributed to earlier work.

after.justification: v2 retains original FCA experiments and reports additional backbone, adapter, ControlNet, and inference-efficiency results, alongside revised human-evaluation outcomes.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.4 retain the parallel attention adapters, frozen DiT conditioning branch, layer-specific text-conditioning modules, attention mask, training objective, and inference procedure. Applying FCA to Wan2.1 adds an evaluated backbone without documenting a changed FCA procedure.

E1.justification: The documented coverage remains text-video prediction on SSv2, BridgeData, and EpicKitchen-100, including the existing instruction-manipulation and failure scenarios. Wan2.1 is an additional model, while InternVid is cited for the evaluator; neither establishes additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds DoRA and AdaLoRA comparisons in Table 11 and pretrained/LoRA-tuned Wan2.1-I2V comparators against FCA on Wan2.1-T2V in Table 10. These extend the adaptation comparisons while retaining the original benchmark comparator sets and ControlNet comparisons.

E3.justification: Human evaluation changes from 24 participants and 15 samples in v1 B.2 to 24 participants and 50 samples in v2 C.2. Added experiments introduce Wan2.1-1.3B configurations and comparative inference timing. Existing benchmark settings remain stable. Table 11's T2V caption conflicts with its I2V rows, leaving that added experiment's exact configuration ambiguous.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends supplementary validation with a test of FCA's generality across backbones, parameter and inference-cost comparisons, and a newly reported LoRA-rank sensitivity finding. Table 12 also supplies quantitative evidence for the existing ControlNet padding ablation. The original FCA component ablations and qualitative failure analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and average human ratings without confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests, or repeated-run/seed information. The human-study sample-count revision changes evaluation design rather than uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 10–12 add FVD results including Wan FCA 72.17, DoRA/AdaLoRA 349.11/305.83, and ControlNet duplicated/zero-padding 529.65/1073.43. Tables 6–8 add resource comparisons. Human ratings change under the larger reported study, including FCA visual fidelity from 3.96 to 3.91. Original Table 1 and VBench scores remain unchanged; these additions do not establish same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, conditioning definitions, attention expression, diffusion objectives, and guidance equations remain equivalent. Neither version adds formal propositions, proofs, or theoretical guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the explicit claim of establishing a new state-of-the-art with establishing a new baseline. The main FCA contributions, claims of outperforming previous work, and stated relative FVD reductions in the introduction remain.

C2.justification: New Section 5 explicitly qualifies FCA's advantages with greater parameter, VRAM, training, and inference costs. v2 also adds a color-distribution conjecture for LoRA failure and interprets VBench overall consistency through ViCLIP text-video alignment. Existing dataset-specific limitations and failure explanations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses LoRA rank 256, parameter counts, comparative inference timings, and Wan checkpoint references. It explicitly describes the retained repository as open-source code. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware, preprocessing, and sampling details remain; the added rank information does not establish a change to earlier runs.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Wan, DoRA, AdaLoRA, and InternVid to support the new comparisons and evaluator explanation. The principal positioning relative to Seer, pretrained video models, and conditioning methods remains. The numerical-to-author-year citation conversion is stylistic.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section ordering are retained. Changes include a standalone Limitations section, additional appendix subsections, updated affiliations, author-year citations, and localized explanatory edits. These do not constitute a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to a single-column layout, extensively resizing and relocating figures and tables. Architecture figures are reordered, six tables are added, and qualitative panels are rearranged. Figure 6 removes the displayed zero-padding example and shows more frames for retained examples; existing appendix examples are largely redisplayed.

improvement.justification: The added backbone and adapter comparisons broaden empirical support, while Section 5 and Tables 6–8 make FCA's resource tradeoffs clearer. These improve assessability beyond v1. The gains remain limited by sparse documentation of added experimental settings and Table 11's conflicting T2V/I2V labels; the central method and original benchmark findings remain unchanged.
